instruction.text: This is a map showing the continents of the world. Select the image that shows Africa.

atoms.b: Africa is made up of 54 countries, with a ((++population area)) of around 1.6 billion people.
Africa is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the ((++west south)) and the Indian Ocean to the east. It is separated from ((++Europe South_America)) by the Mediterranean Sea.
Algeria is the ((++largest smallest)) country in Africa and is found in the very north of the continent.
The Seychelles is the ((++smallest largest)) country in Africa. It is a group of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.label: Imaginary lines
hint.text: The Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn are imaginary lines circling the Earth. The Equator is in the middle and divides the globe into its Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Tropic of Cancer is located to the north of the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn is located to the south.

atoms.text: Africa is the second-largest continent in the world and is located in both the Northern and Southern Hemisphere. As it covers such a large area, its different regions experience very different climates.
Countries north of the Tropic of Cancer experience a dry climate with high temperatures and very little rainfall.
Countries near the Equator have a tropical climate with hot and humid conditions all year round. They have a dry season with less rain and a wet season with regular, heavy downpours.

Moving further south, most regions return to a dry climate. As we near the temperate zone at the southernmost point of the continent, some areas experience a Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild winters.

Which countries in Africa have a tropical climate?
b: countries north of the Tropic of Cancer
countries south of the Tropic of Capricorn

sound.end: Cape Town has a Mediterranean climate.
Zanzibar City has a tropical climate.

atoms.b: Compared to other continents, Africa has many more country borders that are completely ((++straight wavy)) lines. This is because they were decided by European colonial countries.

The borders were drawn onto maps around 150 years ago by European leaders without asking the people living there. This has led to ((++instability stability)), disputes and the separation of communities.
For example, the border between Kenya and Tanzania runs directly through the land of the Maasai people, forcing them to live in two ((++separate identical)) countries.
